why: pricing.py API. Source CSVs store price_cents (int) and discount_pct (whole percent); pricing converts to team convention (dollars, fractions). Region is needed by tax.py to determine sales tax, so get_customer exposes it as a plain string code. Lookups return None when not found.

Returns the tax in integer cents.
why: tax.py needs per-line category and amount to apply exemptions, plus the customer's region and discount. Pricing (agent1) owns the customer data, so pricing or invoice passes these values in; tax.py does not read pricing data.

value: region=None -> tax 0 (per RULES.md). An unknown region string (not in rates.csv) -> KeyError (team lookup rule). Pricing must raise KeyError for an unknown customer ID, so tax only sees None when the customer record exists but has no region.
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, which conflicts with the team rule that a lookup that finds nothing raises KeyError. This split keeps both.

value: Tax computed with integer arithmetic (Decimal or integers, no float): base = taxable_cents * (100 - discount_pct) / 100; tax = base * tax_pct / 100, rounded half up to the cent.
why: Team standard is integer cents and percent numbers. RULES.md specifies half-up rounding; floats would give wrong cent results on exact .5 cases.

Units conflict with pricing_api (my proposal): pricing returns money as float dollars and percentages as fractions (team convention). That keeps tax's integer arithmetic and avoids cross-module unit conversion. Alternatively, if you prefer cents, say so and I will return price_cents as int and discount as whole percent; but the unit must be the same in all modules.

value: rate_pct(region: str | None) -> str: the nominal sales-tax percent for the region as a decimal string without a percent sign, e.g. "8.25" for TX or "0" for region None. Unknown non-None region -> KeyError (same as compute_tax).
why: Invoice must print the Tax percent (e.g. Tax (8.25%)). compute_tax returns only the amount in cents, so invoice.py needs the nominal rate separately. A string avoids float formatting problems; invoice.py normalizes the trailing zeros. If tax exemptions change the effective rate, the displayed percent is still the nominal region rate.
